content: Hi how can i assist you today
Auto-brightness jumps brighter when I think 'brighter,' even without touching the phone.
Ambient light sensors react to reflections, screen content, and angle. Did the screen show a lighter image or tilt toward a light source at that moment?
I rotated toward a window as I was thinking it.
A window can spike the sensor reading. Indoors, does the behavior lessen under steady lighting?
Under a desk lamp it stays steady unless I open a white page.
White pages raise overall luminance, which tends to nudge brightness up.
So content and angle are doing the work.
Those inputs commonly drive auto-brightness changes.
